newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Privatization bonds to be accepted in Banerj sale.
newsitem.headline: Privatization bonds to be accepted in Banerj sale.

text.p: Investors prequalified to participate in the sell-off of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj and its insurance firm will be allowed to use privatization bonds in the auction, according to the tender details published today.

Bidders will have the right to pay 30 million reais -- 27 million reais of Banerj's minimum price and 3.0 million reais of insurer Banerj Seguros' base price -- in Privatization Certificates, which represent state securitized debt.
Banerj and its insurance company will be sold at a minimum prices of 436.693 million reais and 43.310 million reais respectively at a closed-envelope privatization auction on December 17.
Investors will be required to buy the bank and the insurer together.

"Although different prices have been set for each company, the bank and the insurer will not be privatized separately," said Rio de Janeiro state Planning Secretary Marco Aurelio Alencar in a statement.

The tender documents also noted that the World Bank's International Finance Corp (IFC) has shown interest in taking part in the privatization by offering loans to the new majority shareholder or by acquiring a stake in Banerj, the Rio planning office said.
Asked about the auction's rules, prequalified companies said they were still studying the bid specifications.

"We are still analysing the tender documents and the minimum price. But interest in Banerj continues," said Nahid Chicani, vice-president of Human Resources, Communications and Governmental Relations of General Electric Brazil unit.
U.S. General Electric Capital Corp is one of the seven companies prequalified to bid on the bank and the insurer.
The others are Bank of Boston's Brazil unit, BBA Creditanstalt, Banco CCF do Brasil, Banco Itau, Bradesco and Companhia de Investimentos Latino-Americana.

Health insurance firm Golden Cross, which prequalified only to participate in Banerj Seguros' sale, will have to join forces with one of the other bidders to buy the company, the Rio planning office said.
According to the tender documents, investors have until December 6 to sign up for the auction, which gives them time to form consortia.
Investors declined to comment on the price, but sources close to some prequalified bidders said Banerj's base price was considered high.
